name: Screen record + reaction
summary: Face cam in a corner reacting to using the app for the first time, with the screen recording full-frame and a reaction peak at the wow moment.

beats.label: Hook on your face
beats.tip: Say the hook while looking at the camera.

beats.label: Use it for the first time
beats.tip: Keep your face cam small in the corner.

beats.label: The wow moment
beats.tip: React honestly when the result lands.

beats.label: Show the result
beats.tip: Hold the result for two seconds.

beats.label: One call to action
beats.tip: Link in bio or your code.

example_script:
[0:00 · face to camera] I was wrong about every app I tried before {app}.
[0:02 · cut to screen recording, face cam in the corner] So I opened {app} for the first time and tapped {feature}.
[0:04 · demo, no cuts] Okay, watching what it does with my own stuff.
[0:14 · reaction] Wait. No. That is exactly what I wanted, in one tap.
[0:18 · result full-frame, hold two seconds] Look at that.
[0:23 · face] There is a free trial, so you can try it before you pay for anything.
[0:26 · face, link on screen] Link in my bio.
shot_list: Face to camera, offer and call to action
why_it_works: Shows the product and a human together, and the reaction is the proof. Named the best-performing app-install format in 2026 by an AI-UGC vendor (reported).

name: Hidden gem
summary: "This app is so slept on." One killer feature on screen, then "and it is free to try".

beats.label: Slept-on hook
beats.tip: Name the feeling: nobody talks about this.

example_script:
[0:00 · face] This app is so slept on, I almost feel bad telling you about it.
[0:03 · screen recording] It is {app}, and it has {feature}.
[0:05 · demo, one feature only] Watch this: one tap and it is done. I do not know how I lived without it.
[0:16 · proof, your real before and after] Before: [your real number]. After: [your real number].
[0:21 · face] And it is free to try, so there is nothing to lose.
[0:24 · face] Link in my bio.
shot_list: Face to camera, offer and call to action
why_it_works: Feels like organic discovery instead of an ad, so it earns attention from cold audiences.

name: Confession hook
summary: "I did not expect to use this app every day, but here we are." Then why, a demo and one call to action.

beats.label: Confession
beats.tip: Specific and slightly funny beats generic.

beats.label: Show the app
beats.tip: Screen recording by 0:10 at the latest.

beats.label: What changed
beats.tip: Show one real moment from your week.

beats.label: Where you are now
beats.tip: Say the result in your own words.

beats.label: One call to action
beats.tip: Use my code or link in bio.

example_script:
[0:00 · face] I did not expect to use {app} every single day, but here we are.
[0:03 · b-roll of the problem] I used to think apps like this were a waste of money. I would download one, forget it and move on.
[0:08 · screen recording] Then I tried {app}.
[0:10 · demo, one real moment from your week] This is {feature}. Last week I used it for [the real thing you did] and it took about a minute.
[0:20 · face] Where am I now? [One honest sentence about the result.] Still using it.
[0:25 · face, code on screen] Use my code or the link in my bio.
shot_list: Face to camera, where you are now
why_it_works: Confession and controversy hooks are reported to beat others for app installs.

name: Problem, solution, result
summary: The pain in one line, the app solving it on screen, the result, one call to action.

beats.label: The pain in one line
beats.tip: This is your hook. Make it feel familiar.

beats.label: Show the app
beats.tip: App on screen by 0:07 at the latest.

beats.label: The result
beats.tip: Show the number or the finished thing.

example_script:
[0:00 · face or b-roll] Every week I lose an hour to [the chore you really hate].
[0:04 · screen recording] Here is how {app} fixes it.
[0:07 · demo, one workflow start to finish] You open it, tap {feature}, and that is the whole job.
[0:17 · result close-up] [Show the number or the finished thing.] That hour is now about five minutes.
[0:23 · face] It is free to try, so you can check my math.
[0:26 · face] Link in my bio.
shot_list: Face or b-roll of the problem
why_it_works: One of the most consistent converting formats: the viewer sees the pain, the fix and the result in 25 seconds.

name: Faceless slideshow
summary: Five to eight slides telling a story or tips; the app appears on slide 4, never first or last. No face needed.

beats.label: Slide 4: the app
beats.tip: Show the app here, never first or last.

beats.label: Last slide: one call to action

example_script:
Slide 1 (0:00): "I tested [five] apps so you do not have to. One stayed."
Slides 2 and 3 (0:03): "Most apps want your attention." / "I only keep the ones that are fast, honest and easy to quit."
Slide 4 (0:09): "{app}" with a screenshot of {feature}.
Slides 5 and 6 (0:13): a screenshot of the result and one real number from your own use.
Slide 7 (0:20): "Free to try. Cancel any time."
Last slide (0:24): "Comment LINK and I will send it."
why_it_works: Carousels outperform many video concepts for organic reach, and no face means more creators can join.

name: Green screen
summary: You in front of the app store page, a viral comment, a screenshot or a stat, talking over it.

beats.label: Hook over the background
beats.tip: Point at the stat or comment.

beats.label: Explain the one thing
beats.tip: Talk to camera over the screenshot.

example_script:
[0:00 · green screen: the store page or a comment, point at it] Someone asked me if {app} is actually worth it.
[0:03 · talk over the screenshot] Here is the thing: it does {feature}, and most apps in this space do not.
[0:12 · cut to your phone] Watch. [Live demo of {feature}, no cuts.]
[0:19 · face] The trial is free and the price after it is on the screen, no surprises.
[0:23 · face] Link in my bio.
shot_list: Green-screen shot over the store page
Face to camera, call to action
why_it_works: Feels native on TikTok and lets the creator argue a point with evidence behind them.

name: Results update
summary: "Day 30 of using the app." Before versus now, then the feature that did it.

beats.label: Day N hook
beats.tip: Say the day count and one real number.

example_script:
[0:00 · face] Day [7 or 30] of using {app}. Here is the real update.
[0:03 · before, on screen] This was me before: [one honest line and a screenshot].
[0:08 · now, on screen] This is me now: [the same screenshot or number, updated].
[0:12 · screen recording] The thing that did it was {feature}.
[0:20 · face] Honestly? [One thing that changed and one thing that did not.]
[0:25 · face] Link in my bio if you want to follow along.
why_it_works: Proof beats claims, and the format serialises into a recurring post (Day 7, Day 30).

name: Identity transformation
summary: "I became someone who..." with the app as the habit behind it.

beats.label: The habit in action
beats.tip: A real moment from the routine.

example_script:
[0:00 · face] I became someone who [the new habit], and I did not see it coming.
[0:03 · b-roll of the old routine] Six months ago I was the person who [the old habit, one honest line].
[0:08 · screen recording] What changed was {app}.
[0:12 · the habit in action] Every [morning or evening] I open it and use {feature}. It takes about [your real time].
[0:20 · face, end on the win] Now I am someone who [the new habit]. Small, but it stuck.
[0:25 · face] Link in my bio.
why_it_works: Recommended for subscription apps, along with leading with the free trial.

name: Free-trial lead
summary: The offer in the first 3 seconds ("try it free for 7 days"), a quick demo, then value per day.

beats.label: Lead with the trial
beats.tip: Say the trial length in the first sentence.

beats.label: Value per day
beats.tip: Say what it costs after, honestly.

example_script:
[0:00 · face] You can try {app} free before paying for anything.
[0:03 · screen recording] Here is what you get in the first minute: {feature}.
[0:06 · quick demo, one feature, fast] Tap, tap, done.
[0:16 · price screen] After the trial it is [read the real price off the app page], and you can cancel in two taps.
[0:21 · face] Try it free. Link in my bio.
why_it_works: Risk reversal reduces the leap to install; recommended for subscription apps.

name: Reply to a comment
summary: Pin a skeptical comment ("does this actually work?") and answer it with a demo.

beats.label: The pinned comment
beats.tip: Show the comment and read it out.

beats.label: The honest answer
beats.tip: Include one limitation to stay credible.

example_script:
[0:00 · reply-to-comment sticker, read it out loud] "Does {app} actually work or is it just hype?"
[0:02 · face] Fair question. Let me show you instead of telling you.
[0:03 · screen recording] This is {feature}. [Live demo, no cuts.]
[0:15 · face] So yes, it works. One honest limit: [name one real thing it does not do].
[0:21 · face] Comment "link" and I will send it.
shot_list: Face to camera, the honest answer
why_it_works: Uses the comment as a built-in hook and answers the objection directly.

name: Carousel turned video
summary: A slideshow rendered as a video with a text block mid-way naming the app.
example_script:
Slide 1 (0:00): "[One promise, one line.]"
Slides 2 to 4 (0:03): three short tips, one idea each.
Slide 5 (0:12): "Made with {app}" over a screenshot of {feature}.
Slides 6 and 7 (0:16): the proof, a screenshot and one real number.
Last slide (0:22): "Link in my bio."
why_it_works: Gets carousel-style storytelling into video placements and paid ads.
